name: figma-edit-mcp
description: Read, create, and modify Figma designs programmatically via MCP, empowering AI to execute Figma changes safer, cleaner, and faster.
long_description:
Connect AI assistants to Figma via Model Context Protocol to read designs, create and modify elements, and manage design systems programmatically.

This plugin empowers your AI assistant to become an active design co-pilot, executing updates and modifications Safer, Cleaner, and Faster than manual entry. By offloading repetitive, error-prone manual operations to automated systems, designers are freed to focus entirely on creative decision-making and product strategy.

### Core Principles

* **🛡️ Safer**: The server enforces robust programmatic checks and validations that exceed the Figma Desktop app's default protections. For instance, it prevents deleting variables currently in use to avoid dangling references. By validating all writes against a locked editable scope and strict name checks before execution, it protects files from human error and AI hallucinations.

* **✨ Cleaner**: System-driven, programmatic operations guarantee that no layers, text nodes, or components are skipped or forgotten during complex updates. Every design file stays consistent and conforms exactly to your design system.

* **⚡ Faster**: Bulk edits like propagating instance overrides, batch-updating copy, or restructuring auto-layout frames are handled via high-performance APIs. Hours of tedious, click-heavy manual work are completed in seconds.

### How it Works (Prerequisites)
This server runs locally on your machine. To operate, it requires:
1. The Figma Desktop App to be open.
2. The `Figma Edit` plugin to be active on the file you want to modify (listening on local port `3845`).

host.title: WebSocket Host
host.description: Host the MCP server uses to reach the Figma plugin

port.title: WebSocket Port
port.description: Port the MCP server uses to reach the Figma plugin

tools.name: page_info
tools.description: List the document's pages; no args → all pages (no children), or pass `pageIds` → those pages with their top-level children. Batch ≤25 ids/call. Inspect `coverage`: a failed page is omitted with a structured `pageErrors` row while other pages still return.

tools.name: node_info
tools.description: Read one or more nodes — recursive subtree traversal with `properties` selection, `filter`, and `maxDepth`. Returns only the requested properties (incl. resolved `boundVariables`/`explicitVariableModes`) under each node's `properties` key. A node whose containing page could not be read is listed in `pageFailedNodes` with that page's ID, and the page's structured reason is in `coverage.pageErrors` — other pages still return normally. The workhorse read; start here before any write.

tools.name: node_transform
tools.description: Move and/or resize a node by setting absolute `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` (any subset).

tools.name: node_rename
tools.description: Rename a node (sets `name` to an exact value).

tools.name: node_delete
tools.description: Delete one or more nodes in a single batched, per-item-validated call. No API undo. If the status is 'partial_success', treat it as an incomplete operation, report the failed and skipped items to the user, and retry every non-success item (both failed and skipped).

tools.name: node_clone
tools.description: Duplicate an existing node, optionally at a new `x`/`y`. Produces a new node id.

tools.name: view_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the editor view to a page or node(s).

tools.name: node_group
tools.description: Wrap multiple nodes in a new group node.

tools.name: node_ungroup
tools.description: Dissolve a group, promoting its children to the parent. Removes the group container.

tools.name: node_flatten
tools.description: Flatten a node and its children into a single vector. Lossy — original structure is not recoverable.

tools.name: node_insert_child
tools.description: Reparent a node under a new parent at an optional `index`. Valid range is 0 to parent's child count. Omit `index` to append.

tools.name: node_set_auto_layout
tools.description: Configure a frame's auto-layout (mode, padding, spacing, alignment, sizing) in one unified setter.

tools.name: node_set_fill
tools.description: Set a node's fill to a literal RGBA color, an image, or clear it. Use `node_apply_style` to link a shared paint style, or `node_bind_variable` to bind a color token.

tools.name: node_set_stroke
tools.description: Set a node's stroke color and weight; supports uniform or per-side weights.

tools.name: node_set_corner_radius
tools.description: Set a node's corner radius — uniform or per-corner.

tools.name: node_set_effects
tools.description: Set a node's effect array (shadows, blurs). Use `node_apply_style` to link a shared effect style instead.

tools.name: node_apply_style
tools.description: Link a node to a shared library style (paint/text/effect/grid) by `styleId`. Use the raw `node_set_*` setters for ad-hoc values not backed by a style.

tools.name: node_bind_variable
tools.description: Bind a variable to a node property, or set an explicit variable mode. Use instead of a literal `node_set_*` when the value should track a design token. Ordering rules: set auto-layout before binding padding/spacing; set a solid fill before binding a colour token.

tools.name: node_export_visual
tools.description: Render a node to an image (PNG/JPG/SVG/PDF) at a given scale. Read-only; the canonical way to visually verify edits. SVG returns raw XML in `svg` (directly readable); PNG/JPG/PDF return base64 in `imageData` (PDF is a delivery artifact — prefer PNG/SVG for inspection).

tools.name: create_shape
tools.description: Create a rectangle, ellipse, polygon, or star via `type`, with position/size and optional `fillColor`/`strokeColor`. Shape-specific params (`arcData`; `pointCount`/`innerRadius`) validated by `type`. `pointCount` = sides (polygon) or points (star), native count — no even-parity rule.

tools.name: create_frame
tools.description: Create a frame (container) with optional fill/stroke and full auto-layout configuration.

tools.name: create_text
tools.description: Create a text node with content and optional font size/weight/color.

tools.name: create_svg
tools.description: Create a node from an SVG markup string.

tools.name: create_component
tools.description: Convert an existing frame into a main component.

tools.name: create_instance
tools.description: Instantiate a component (by `componentKey` or `componentId`) at a position.

tools.name: create_component_set
tools.description: Combine components into a component set (variants) with property definitions.

tools.name: style_list
tools.description: List all local styles (paint/text/effect/grid) in the document.

tools.name: style_manage
tools.description: Create a named style (paint/text/effect/grid), or update an existing one when `styleId` is given. UPDATE requires currentStyleName.

tools.name: style_delete
tools.description: Delete a local style by id. Detaches consumers — they keep their resolved values and lose only the style link.

tools.name: text_set_content
tools.description: Set the text of one or more text nodes in a single batched, per-item-validated call. If the status is 'partial_success', treat it as an incomplete operation, report the failed and skipped items to the user, and retry every non-success item (both failed and skipped).

tools.name: text_set_style
tools.description: Set any combination of typography properties (font, size, weight, spacing, decoration, …) on a text node.

tools.name: component_list
tools.description: List components in the document, with filtering and scope options. Document scans isolate page failures and report them in `coverage`; page-scoped failures return their structured error directly.

tools.name: component_manage_property
tools.description: Add or edit a component-property definition (BOOLEAN/TEXT/INSTANCE_SWAP) on a main component or variant set. Deleting is `component_delete_property`.

tools.name: component_delete_property
tools.description: Remove a component-property definition from a main component or variant set; propagates to every instance.

tools.name: instance_set_property
tools.description: Set one property on an instance — boolean toggle, text override, instance swap, or variant selection.

tools.name: instance_get_overrides
tools.description: Read the override properties from a source instance, to later apply them to other instances.

tools.name: instance_set_overrides
tools.description: Apply previously-read overrides to target instances; targets are swapped to the source component and all overrides applied. If the status is 'partial_success', treat it as an incomplete operation, report the failed and skipped items to the user, and retry every non-success item (both failed and skipped).

tools.name: variable_list
tools.description: List local variables/collections, or detailed info for specific variable ids; optionally scan for consumers. Document consumer scans isolate page failures and report them in `coverage`; page-scoped failures return their structured error directly.

tools.name: variable_manage
tools.description: Create collections and variables and set their values/aliases (create/update router). UPDATE_VARIABLE requires `currentVariableName`. CREATE_VARIABLE requires `collectionName` and `scopes`.

tools.name: variable_delete
tools.description: Delete specific variables or an entire collection. Runs a full-document consumer check first, before any removal: if a target is still in use the call is refused with VARIABLE_IN_USE, whose `details.variablesInUse` lists every consumer; if any page cannot be loaded and read it is refused with DOCUMENT_SCAN_INCOMPLETE, because a page error can never mean zero consumers.

tools.name: annotation_list
tools.description: Read the native annotations on a page or node (and subtree); exactly one of pageId or nodeId is required. Optionally include the file's annotation categories. Page loading is bounded; a page-scoped failure returns its structured error directly and successful reads include `coverage`.

tools.name: annotation_set
tools.description: Append native annotations to one or more nodes in a batched call. If the status is 'partial_success', treat it as an incomplete operation and report the failed and skipped items to the user. Appending is NOT idempotent and a 'failed' row may already have appended its annotation (verified counts differ, or outcomeUnknown is true when post-state is unreadable; both carry partialMutation: true) — before retrying any non-success item, call annotation_list and compare the labels already on the node, or you will create a duplicate.

tools.name: reaction_list
tools.description: Read prototype reactions from one or more nodes and their descendants.

tools.name: reaction_update
tools.description: Replace a node's prototype reactions with a full new reactions array (read first via `reaction_list`).

tools.name: channel_join
tools.description: Join a plugin channel to establish the live connection to the Figma document.
